To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
synthetic T1- or T2-weighted brain MR in children is diagnostically acceptable with equal or better image quality and gray/white contrast, but synthetic FLIR is not diagnostically acceptable.
synthetic T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI in children are diagnostically acceptable and comparable to conventional MRI in image quality, gray-white matter differentiation and lesion conspicuity.
synthetic MRI is an alternative to conventional MRI for children.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the quality of synthetic brain MRI in children.
the development of a novel imaging technique for brain MRI, which is based on synthetic MRI.
the quality of synthetic brain magnetic resonance (MR) imaging in children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the quality of the T1- and the T2-weighted synthetic images was comparable or superior to the quality of the conventional images.
synthetic T1- or T2-weighted sequences are diagnostically acceptable in children, but synthetic FLIR sequences are not.
synthetic MRI is a feasible alternative to conventional MRI in children.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
synthetic imaging is a promising tool to reduce scan time in pediatric MRI, but further research is needed to improve the image quality, especially in the FLAIR sequence.
the image quality of T1-weighted images is comparable to conventional T1-weighted MRI, while the image quality of FLAIR images is not comparable to conventional FLAIR MRI.
synthetic MRI is a promising alternative for brain imaging in children.
The main takeaway from our work is that
synthetic MRI can be used in pediatric brain MR imaging.
synthetic T1- and T2-weighted brain MRI in children is feasible, but synthetic FLair images are not.
the use of the synthetic technique for brain MR is promising, but the quality of the synthetic FLAIR image needs to be improved.
